Container.Name: LazyBackup
Container.Overview:
LazyBackup is a From → To backup manager: pick a source, pick a destination, set a cron schedule, and it runs — no scripts and no per-app glue.
Sources: filesystem paths, Docker volumes, PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / SQLite dumps, Git repositories as bare mirrors, or LazyBackup itself (SQLite database, age vault and SSH keys). Destinations: this host, SSH servers, S3-compatible storage (MinIO, R2, B2, AWS) and Bro Space — encrypted, quota-limited space on a friend's LazyBackup or LazyBro instance.
Includes versioned snapshots with count-based retention, age encryption with a key vault and recovery recipients, one-click restore from History (optionally onto another host), failure webhooks (Discord, Telegram, ntfy, Slack, Uptime Kuma), success pings, an app password or WebAuthn passkeys, and a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint for agents.
App data lives in /app/data and local backups in /backups. Remote servers need SSH key authentication (mount the keys folder read-only). The container runs as root, so files it writes are owned by root. Set an app password or a passkey before exposing the WebUI.
Container.Requires:
SSH key authentication on every server used in a transfer. rsync, scp, git, sqlite3 and curl are bundled with the image.
Local Docker-volume packing and docker exec database dumps need the Docker CLI and /var/run/docker.sock, which this image does not ship; use a remote Docker host over SSH for those. PostgreSQL and MySQL client tools are not bundled either, so SQLite is the only natively dumped local database.
Set AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true only when the UI is served over HTTPS (prefer HSTS at the reverse proxy).
Container.Changes: Initial Community Applications submission (v0.4.1). Bro Space rebuilt around friends with confirmed delivery, restore from the run's own snapshot, chunked peer restores, atomic database and fixed volume restores, pre-backup commands that fail the run, and a security pass (CSRF, step-up auth, SSRF, option injection).
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: backup rsync ssh s3 docker volume database postgres mysql mariadb sqlite git mirror encryption age peer restore cron retention webhook

Config.Name: App data
Config.Description: SQLite database, instance settings, age vault and SSH known_hosts.

Config.Name: Backup storage
Config.Description: Default root for backups written to this host.

Config.Name: SSH keys
Config.Description: Read-only directory with the SSH keys used for rsync/scp/git to remote servers. Point it at a dedicated folder, not the whole ~/.ssh.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: SQLite URL inside the container. Keep it on the App data path or the database is lost when the container is recreated.

Config.Name: BACKUP_STORAGE_PATH
Config.Description: In-container root for backups landing on this host. Matches the Backup storage path.

Config.Name: AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE
Config.Description: Set to true only when the UI is served over HTTPS; on plain HTTP leave it empty or login breaks.

Config.Name: AUTH_PUBLIC_URL
Config.Description: Exact public origin (for example https://backup.example.com) so passkeys work behind a reverse proxy.

Config.Name: AUTH_TRUST_PROXY
Config.Description: Set to true only behind a proxy that overwrites X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For.

Config.Name: ENABLE_HSTS
Config.Description: Set to true only when every request is HTTPS. HSTS at the reverse proxy is usually better.
